title: Separate bootstrap administrator identity from hosted mail domains

costar.context: Owner selected a reserved system domain and independent control-plane administrator.
costar.objective: Seed the reserved domain and first root administrator without creating a real mail domain, and protect the boundary through account/domain management.
costar.response: Committed main changes with unchanged release version and explicit verification limits

concerns: Root must still provision normal mail users: removing its grantable permissions would prevent that, so deny mail use at the token capability boundary while preserving permission delegation checks.
A reserved domain must not be reassigned, renamed, aliased, deleted or enabled for DNS/certificate automation through general registry APIs.
Global external authentication directories must not take over system-domain credentials.
Bootstrap must be idempotent and fail explicitly on a conflicting reserved name without overwriting existing data.
Fresh installs receive the reserved default; existing explicit defaults and mail accounts are not silently migrated.
Mail reports and alerts must not use the reserved identity domain as a public sender; system('domain') uses the configured server hostname when the identity default is reserved.

The pre-existing short-name fixture shut workers down before cleanup and waited on 30-day retention. Run this authentication fixture with zero retention, retain its cleanup assertion, bound its wait, and stop workers afterward; product retention stays unchanged.

Candidate-image first-run browser, full mail interoperability/recovery, cluster failure recovery and PostgreSQL-to-FoundationDB transfer remain separate qualification requirements; backend integration is not full release readiness.
context: Baseline main 1b39550; no product release/tag changes are authorized.
current_state: Setup requires a real address and creates its domain. No protected system domain exists. Account domainId is mandatory.
target_design: Persistent bootstrap seeds system.local with manual DNS/DKIM/certificates and sets a new installation's defaultDomainId to it. First-run setup creates root@system.local from a password-only request. Reserved domain is immutable through ordinary management. System identities use local authentication, cannot acquire real-domain aliases or tenant membership, and cannot use SMTP/IMAP/POP3/ManageSieve or receive mail. Root retains account/domain administration and delegation. Real domains remain separately managed tenant data.
changes: Add a reserved-domain bootstrap helper and policy functions with unit tests.
Enforce reserved domain/account boundaries in registry validation and domain deletion; protect the seeded defaultDomainId.
Separate system account mail-use restrictions from grantable administration permissions and exclude the system domain from external directory routing/SMTP recipients.
Replace first-run email selection with a fixed root identity in the existing Svelte setup screen and password-only API.
Update API/deploy documentation and first-run/integration tests covering root login, permission boundaries and real-domain lifecycle.
Keep default identity resolution separate from public mail-report/alert sender defaults; preserve existing real default-domain behavior.
Regenerate stale compressed login/RSVP assets from their existing minified sources after the full HTTP suite exposed old /api routes in the served payloads.
boundaries: No legacy compatibility layer, real-user deployment, release tag or version change.
Keep PostgreSQL first, FoundationDB scale, storage versatility and existing mail capabilities for real mail accounts.
Do not rename/delete existing mail domains or migrate existing administrator identities automatically.

verification.name: Runtime build and unit tests
verification.command: cargo test -p common --lib --locked; cargo test -p http@0.16.27 --lib --locked; cargo check -p shippin-tech --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,s3,nats,enterprise
verification.proves: Bootstrap policy, request contract and protocol-use/delegation separation compile and behave correctly
verification.expected: Relevant tests and application check pass
verification.result: Windows: 164 common tests passed; 36 HTTP tests passed after regenerating two stale compressed assets; PostgreSQL/S3/NATS/enterprise application check passed. No Cargo versions or lockfile changes. Logs in ignored target/system-domain-{common-tests,http-tests,postgres-check}.log.

verification.name: Whole web/deploy gate
verification.expected: All available checks pass; missing coverage reported
verification.result: 18 available checks passed, zero failures: 289 UI unit tests, 13 mocked browser tests, typecheck, build, lint, API/brand/registry/MCPL/inventory and deploy checks. Relay is not run by the Windows runner because its permissions assertions require POSIX. Live/image steps omitted, not passed. Evidence roadmap/regression-results.partial.json (ignored). The relay shell suite subsequently passed in Linux Docker (target/system-domain-backend-tests.log); all 19 web/deploy checks now have passing observations across the two environments.

verification.name: Integrated first-run and domain lifecycle
verification.command: Linux Docker: RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 shippin.tech_KEEP_DELETED_DAYS=0 STORE=PostgreSql (then Sqlite) cargo test -p tests --locked --no-default-features --features sqlite,postgres system::authentication -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
verification.proves: Reserved bootstrap/default and store reopen; root setup API/key retirement; mail-use/delegation separation; real-domain lifecycle; short-name ambiguity and account isolation on each backend
verification.expected: Three tests pass per backend; image-level live browser/protocol/recovery remain explicitly unverified
verification.result: Linux Docker, Rust 1.100.0, PostgreSQL 16-alpine: 3 passed, 0 failed in 7.50s; SQLite: 3 passed, 0 failed in 7.93s. Store handles are dropped/reopened before reseeding. First PostgreSQL debug test run overflowed the default worker stack; final run and CI use RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216. Auth fixtures use KEEP_DELETED_DAYS=0 for bounded cleanup, without altering product retention. Log: target/system-domain-backend-tests.log. Protocol checks exercise access-token enforcement and recipient resolution, not independent mail-client socket sessions.
